missing_evidence: No agenda, minutes, participant roster, or city-directory listing is supplied, so whether the Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council is a chartered City of Fort Worth body versus a body whose proceedings the city records cannot be confirmed from the supplied evidence alone; per the sparse policy this gap does not make the recording non-city, and per the proof policy it does not prove exclusion. No second convener is named in any supplied evidence, so no additional joint-meeting participant is proven; the identity policy bars inferring joint convocation from shared members, venue, or topic.
A.rationale: The sole supplied official evidence (provider-player, clip_id=2469, view_id=11 on fortworthgov.granicus.com) titles the 2016-02-13 clip 'Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council' and shows the same name as the player's archive category. The doubled body label is a source duplication artifact; the official name is 'Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council'. That official title establishes the one proven participant and owner of the recording. Reviewing all 54 existing feeds, none is configured for this body. Topic-similar feeds belong to different convened bodies and are rejected under the identity policy (convened body, not topic words or common members): 'fort-worth-tx-minority-and-women-business-enterprise-advisory-committee' (a distinct advisory committee), 'fort-worth-tx-human-relations-commission', and 'fort-worth-tx-race-and-culture-task-force' are not this body; 'fort-worth-tx-public-info-meetings' is a family feed for proven public-information bodies, which this clip's evidence does not establish; the general 'fort-worth-tx' feed is described as FWTV City Council recordings, and this is not a City Council proceeding. No feed slug is invented. Under the sparse policy, a real body without an existing feed is unconfigured rather than non-city, so the publication action is unconfigured_body, naming the Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council for feed configuration; the recording is not declared non-government, as it is published in the City of Fort Worth's official Granicus archive. archive_only, archive_series, and exclude_event do not apply: the supplied evidence shows a body meeting, not a promotional/orientation film, economic-development luncheon, ceremony, dedication, or candidate forum, so no general exclusion rule is met. Because the official title establishes ownership by the named body, the case is unconfigured_body rather than unresolved.

missing_evidence: No agenda, minutes, membership roster, or convening order in the supplied evidence establishing 'Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council' as a municipal body or program convened by the City of Fort Worth.

No evidence distinguishing this named entity from similarly titled but distinct configured bodies (e.g., fort-worth-tx-minority-and-women-business-enterprise-advisory-committee) or linking it to any existing feed slug.

No evidence of City of Fort Worth sponsorship or convening versus third-party use of the city's Granicus platform; hosting alone does not establish ownership, as non-city bodies are hosted in this archive (cf. the Trinity Metro Board feed description).
No content evidence (video index, agenda packet, or episode details) that would support applying the archive_only, archive_series, or exclude_event publication rules.
B.rationale: The sole supplied evidence (provider-player) is the Fort Worth Granicus MediaPlayer page for clip_id=2469 dated 2016-02-13, whose official metadata names the recording 'Minority Leaders and Citizen's Council' (title/label duplicated in the metadata). This proves only the stated name; it contains no agenda, minutes, membership, or convening documentation establishing it as a municipal body or program of Fort Worth rather than an external organization streamed on the city platform. Hosting in fortworthgov.granicus.com alone does not establish ownership, since non-city bodies are hosted in this archive (e.g., Trinity Metro Board per its feed description). The name matches no existing feed slug, and under the identity rule (convened body, not topic or similarity) it cannot be assigned to the similarly named but distinct Minority and Women Business Enterprise Advisory Committee or any other configured body. No joint participants are evidenced, so none are named. Per the proof policy, missing ownership proof requires unresolved and does not prove exclusion; per the sparse policy, a real body without a feed would be unconfigured, but even that status first requires establishing it as a real municipal body, which this evidence does not do. Empty feeds alone do not make this a non-meeting, and no content evidence supports archive_only, archive_series, or exclude_event. No feed slug is assigned, no institution is invented, and the recording is not declared non-government; if later evidence proves a City body/program, it would be unconfigured_body, and if it proves to be a candidate forum or luncheon, the series/archive rules would apply.

policy.archive: Promotional/orientation films and economic-development luncheons are archive-only.
policy.events: Ceremonies, dedications and their site-tour segments are excluded from body feeds.
policy.families: Use configured bond/TIF/public-information family feeds for their proven bodies.
policy.identity: Use the convened body, not venue, topic or common members; numbered boards differ.
policy.joints: Every proven participant can share the same recording in its configured feed.
policy.proof: Missing ownership proof requires unresolved; it does not prove exclusion.
policy.public_comment: Routine public comment does not add Public Info feed membership.
policy.series: Candidate forums remain archival series, not Council proceedings.
policy.sparse: A real body without an existing feed is unconfigured, not automatically non-city.

missing_evidence: The only supplied evidence (provider-player) is a Granicus player page whose text contains just the episode title 'Fort Worth Forward - Episode 15' and generic player controls; no agenda, description, credits, or body metadata identifies the municipal body that convenes, hosts, or produces this program.
No official evidence links this episode to any body with an existing feed (e.g., State of the City, Public Info Meetings, City Council), so no feed assignment can be proven.
A.rationale: The supplied evidence shows only the title 'Fort Worth Forward - Episode 15' on a Fort Worth Granicus player page. That title names a program/series, not a convened municipal body, and the identity rule forbids inferring the body from topic words or the city name. Nothing in the evidence establishes ownership by any specific body, so per the proof policy the correct action is 'unresolved': I do not invent an institution, do not assign an existing feed slug, and do not declare the recording non-government. I also cannot apply archive_only, because the promotional/orientation classification itself is unproven — the episode could equally be a council-produced informational program or a State of the City-style address, but no supplied evidence distinguishes these. If evidence such as an agenda, program description, or producing-department metadata is later supplied identifying the actual body or program, that body can be named and mapped to its configured feed (or unconfigured_body if none exists).

missing_evidence: No agenda, minutes, or content description; evidence provider-player supplies only the Granicus player page and the series title 'Fort Worth Forward - Episode 15' (Documents list contains only a 'Default Document')
No evidence identifies a convening municipal body, producing department, or series credits that could confirm or contradict the promotional-series classification
B.rationale: The only supplied evidence (provider-player) is the City's Granicus player page for a recording titled 'Fort Worth Forward - Episode 15' (2023-02-28), with no agenda, minutes, or attached documents. The numbered-episode title format identifies a recurring produced media series rather than a proceeding of any municipal body: no council, board, commission, committee, or other convener is named, and the evidence shows no meeting or participants. Under the approved publication rules, promotional/orientation films are archive-only; a city-branded episodic program such as 'Fort Worth Forward' falls under that rule. No existing feed corresponds to this series and none may be invented, and the citywide 'fort-worth-tx' feed is limited to City Council meeting videos, so no feed slug applies. The recording is retained in the official city archive — it is not excluded and not declared non-government — but is published to no body feed. No municipal body is proven, so 'bodies' is empty; 'Fort Worth Forward' is treated as a promotional series title, not a real body, so unconfigured_body does not apply.
